articles.titulo: A natural mutation of timeless enhances mosquito thermal adaptation and malaria parasite transmission.
articles.autores: Wang G, Sun P, … Wang S (18 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Anopheles stephensi, a malaria-transmitting mosquito, has invaded Africa and rapidly adapts to the high temperatures in urban settings. However, the molecular basis of its thermal adaptation remains unclear. Here, we identified a variant of a 5-kb deletion in the circadian clock gene timeless (tim-5kb) that rose to high frequency after 3 years of rearing at high laboratory temperatures. The tim+/-5kb heterozygous males maintain stable expression of the period gene at high temperatures, conferring a competitive mating advantage through the increased expression of the adipokinetic hormone gene AKH1 to promote energy mobilization and flight activity, together with the upregulation of fatty acyl-CoA reductase genes FAR3 and FAR5 to enhance the production of heptacosane pheromone. Moreover, heterozygous females exhibit increased susceptibility to Plasmodium infection, increasing malaria transmission potential. These findings reveal a circadian-based genetic mechanism that may underlie thermal adaptation in An. stephensi and hold important implications for malaria control in Africa.

v6.implicacao: Para Alimentação sanguínea de Aedes / Imunometabolismo (tema competência vetorial) e Malária / Plasmodium: a temperatura de criação seleciona uma variante de relógio que liga um hormônio metabólico (AKH1) a maior suscetibilidade ao parasito; temperatura de insectário e deriva genética da colônia viram variáveis de competência a registrar.
v6.resumo: Em colônia de An. stephensi mantida a temperatura alta por 3 anos, surgiu uma deleção de 5 kb em timeless (tim-5kb). Machos heterozigotos mantêm period estável no calor, expressam mais AKH1 (mobilização de energia, voo) e FAR3/FAR5 (feromônio heptacosano) e ganham no acasalamento; fêmeas heterozigotas ficam mais suscetíveis a Plasmodium.
v6.metodo: Sequenciamento da colônia ao longo do tempo para achar a variante, depois ensaios de acasalamento, expressão gênica e infecção por Plasmodium em heterozigotos.

articles.titulo: A Standardized Rearing Procedure for Aedes aegypti (Diptera: Culicidae): Implications for Laboratory-Based Vector Competence and Control Studies.
articles.autores: Asgarian TS, Moosa-Kazemi SH, … Sedaghat MM (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Aedes aegypti is a major vector of numerous arboviruses, including dengue, Zika, chikungunya and yellow fever. This study aimed to establish a standardized and practical procedure for maintaining and propagating an Ae. aegypti colony under controlled insectary conditions in Bandar Abbas, Iran.
Environmental parameters were routinely monitored. Larvae were reared with an appropriate diet under a regular feeding schedule, while adult mosquitoes were provided with a sucrose solution and blood meals. The correlation between the duration of egg paper drying and the hatching percentage was evaluated. Hatching rates were compared across three media: cooled boiled water, yeast and larval food.
A strong negative correlation was observed between drying duration and hatching percentage, with a Pearson correlation of -0.818 (p< 0.001). Gradual drying of egg papers over a period of two days resulted in a hatching rate of over 90% without any hatching stimulant. No significant differences in hatching rates were found among the three media, as indicated by F= 0.601 (p= 0.578). In a novel observation, female mosquitoes were found to deposit approximately 20-30% of their eggs directly on the water surface inside ovitraps under insectary conditions in Iran.
This study provides a reliable, low-cost model for rearing Ae. aegypti in research insectaries and facilitates future studies on vector control.

v6.resumo: Procedimento padronizado de criação de Ae. aegypti em insectário (Irã): secar o papel de ovos gradualmente por dois dias dá eclosão acima de 90% sem estimulante (r de Pearson -0,818 entre tempo de secagem e eclosão). 💡 Parâmetro simples a conferir na colônia da Plataforma de Insetos Vetores.

articles.titulo: Entomological survey for potential Anopheles malaria vectors and their insecticide resistance status in agricultural and peri-urban sites of Central and Southern Greece.
articles.autores: Balaska S, Parnassa V, … Kioulos I (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Greece has eliminated malaria for several decades now, however the ecological settings as being transformed in response to climatic crisis and the current geo-political situation may pose an epidemiological risk. Evidence on Anopheles vector species occurrence and their insecticide resistance (IR) profile in the country is limited and this study aims to narrow this gap. To this end, Anopheles collections were performed in selected agricultural and peri-urban sites throughout Greece, during 2021-2024. Α sub-set of the populations was assessed for their response to insecticides commonly used in the country, showing evidence of resistance to deltamethrin in Corinthia and Boeotia, and possible resistance for the Phthiotis collection, based on CDC guidelines, while all the characterized populations showed a tendency towards susceptibility to the bacterial larvicide Bti (WHO larval bioassays). A multi-locus DNA barcoding approach identified totally five Anopheles species, with distinct abundances and distribution patterns, including epidemiologically relevant malaria vectors, such as An. sacharovi, Αn. labranchiae and An. claviger. In parallel, monitoring of common pyrethroid resistance-associated mutations in the voltage-gated sodium channel gene revealed the exclusive presence of the wild-type allele L1014. Lastly, a Plasmodium parasite detection assay was applied in the adult Anopheles specimens from Phthiotis producing negative results. In all, our survey updates the Anopheles species distribution map of central and southern Greece and provides valuable evidence on populations' IR status, to support future vector control targeted initiatives. The presence of malaria competent vector species, along with sporadic deltamethrin resistance records, stress the importance of systematic monitoring practices to maintain malaria transmission elimination.

v6.resumo: Levantamento entomológico de vetores Anopheles e status de resistência a inseticida em área agrícola.

articles.titulo: Provenance and competence for CHIKV and DENV of Aedes albopictus populations.
articles.autores: Piccinno R, Madec Y, … Malacrida AR (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Aedes albopictus is one of the world's most hazardous invasive species, increasingly implicated in the autochthonous transmission of Chikungunya (CHIKV) and Dengue (DENV) viruses in newly colonized areas. Since invading the Mediterranean Basin several in the early 1980s, recurrent introductions of distinct lineages have driven extensive genomic admixture within adventive populations. This study investigates whether and how the complex dynamics of these diverse genetic backgrounds have shaped variations in vector competence for CHIKV, DENV, and Zika (ZIKV) viruses.
Using highly polymorphic simple sequence repeat (SSR) markers, we genotyped Ae. Albopictus samples from an ancestral population (Guangzhou, China) and ten adventive populations across five Mediterranean regions (Southern Switzerland, Northern/Central Italy, the Balkans, and Greece). Genetic ancestry and demographic histories were inferred using Bayesian STRUCTURE (v2.3.2.0) and DIYABC-RF. The association between population ancestry and vector competence for CHIKV (06.21), DENV-1, and ZIKV (PE243) was assessed using infection rate, dissemination efficiency, and transmission efficiency indices, analyzed via univariate and multivariate models.
Combining historical records with demographic models revealed that the establishment of Ae. Albopictus in the Mediterranean was driven by chaotic, discontinuous lineage introductions and admixture events, resulting in high spatial and ancestry heterogeneity. Notably, this genetic heterogeneity significantly influences vector competence, in particular for CHIKV and DENV. Interestingly, populations in neighboring geographical areas with distinct ancestries exhibited drastically different competence profiles, whereas geographically distant populations sharing genetic ancestry displayed similar vector competence for CHIKV and DENV.
Our findings demonstrate that the complex population dynamics and colonization history of Ae. Albopictus contributes to variation in vector competence, altering the geographical landscape of arboviral risk. These results underscore the urgent need for localized, geographically tailored vector control strategies in Europe, a region facing a rising trend of both imported and autochthonous arboviral infections.

v6.implicacao: Para Epidemiologia de Precisão: no estudo comparativo de competência vetorial de Aedes aegypti nos seis recortes do município, a ancestralidade genética da população local é um confundidor a medir antes de atribuir diferença de competência a ambiente ou Wolbachia.
v6.resumo: Populações de Ae. albopictus do Mediterrâneo têm ancestralidade heterogênea (introduções descontínuas e miscigenação). Essa ancestralidade explica diferenças de competência para CHIKV e DENV: populações vizinhas com ancestrais distintos diferem muito; populações distantes com mesma ancestralidade se parecem.
v6.metodo: Genotipagem por SSR de uma população ancestral (Guangzhou) e dez adventícias; STRUCTURE e DIYABC-RF; infecção experimental com CHIKV, DENV-1 e ZIKV e índices de infecção, disseminação e transmissão.

articles.titulo: Profiling Histone Modifications in Harpegnathos saltator Brains by CUT&Tag.
articles.autores: Kuang M, Antonova A, … Bonasio R (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Harpegnathos saltator ants are a powerful model for studying socially induced adult brain plasticity. In this species, adult workers can transition into reproductive gamergates, which is accompanied by extensive behavioral, physiological, and gene regulatory changes arising from a single genome. Understanding the chromatin mechanisms that regulate these transitions requires epigenomic methods that are sensitive enough to profile small organs such as insect brains. Cleavage under targets and tagmentation (CUT&Tag) is a genome-wide chromatin profiling method that can be used to map histone modifications at high resolution from low-input samples by using an antibody-directed protein A/G-Tn5 transposase to perform targeted, in situ DNA tagmentation, substantially improving the signal-to-noise ratio compared with other chromatin profiling approaches. Here, we provide a CUT&Tag protocol that has been optimized for profiling histone modifications in Harpegnathos brains. We describe the steps for nuclei isolation from insect brains, followed by antibody incubation, transposase binding and tagmentation, and library preparation for high-throughput sequencing. This protocol is further adaptable to single-cell multiomic assays, enabling high-resolution profiling of the epigenomic landscape in social insect brains and other organs.

v6.resumo: 🎲 [exploração] Protocolo CUT&Tag para modificações de histona em cérebros de formiga (Harpegnathos), com isolamento de núcleos de órgão pequeno e baixa entrada. 💡 Mesma lógica aplica-se a mosquito e à frente de histonas e priming (mini-review Frontiers).
v6.metodo: Isolamento de núcleos, anticorpo, proteína A/G-Tn5, tagmentação in situ e preparo de biblioteca.

articles.titulo: NET-Inhibiting Bio-Orthogonal Gelated Neutrophils Reverse Maladaptive Trained Immunity and Protect Against Periodontitis Recurrence.
articles.autores: Li F, Li X, … He XT (20 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Maladaptive trained immunity (MTI) establishes pathogenic innate immune memory that amplifies the immune response to recurrent chronic inflammatory diseases such as periodontitis, but erasing this memory remains challenging. In this study, we identified neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) as key mediators of periodontitis-induced MTI that reprogrammed bone marrow epigenetics and transcriptomics to amplify inflammation upon secondary challenge. Thus, we designed a NET-inhibiting bioengineered platform (tPA@AGNs-DNase I) to erase MTI and prevent recurrent inflammation. This platform was constructed by encapsulating tPA within activated gelated neutrophils (AGNs) and conjugating DNase I onto the surface by glycoengineering and click chemistry. Leveraging the inflammation-homing property of AGNs, the platform enabled co-delivery of two enzymes: DNase I degraded the DNA scaffold of NETs, while tPA disrupted fibrin‒neutrophil engagement to block NETosis, thereby achieving synergistic NET clearance. Local periodontal administration of tPA@AGNs-DNase I not only resolved primary inflammation but also reversed established MTI by restoring aberrant bone marrow epigenetic and transcriptional reprogramming, thereby markedly attenuating recurrent hyperinflammation and alveolar bone loss in a religature-induced periodontitis model. Collectively, this work provides a bioengineered platform that erases central MTI via in situ NET clearance, offering a paradigm-shifting strategy to control chronic inflammatory disease recurrence.

v6.resumo: Neutrófilos e NETs mantêm imunidade treinada maladaptativa em periodontite, com reprogramação epigenética da medula; plataforma de neutrófilos gelatinados com DNase I e tPA apaga a memória e evita recidiva. 💡 Prova de conceito de que a memória inata é apagável por intervenção sobre um mediador, útil para pensar um controle negativo de reversão do priming em Aag2.

articles.titulo: Itaconate as a central node in immunometabolism and inflammatory control.
articles.autores: Lin J, Wang G, Zi F (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Mitochondria serve as central regulators of cellular bioenergetics and inflammatory signaling, integrating metabolic status with immune responses. Disruption of mitochondrial homeostasis, including altered tricarboxylic acid cycle dynamics, redox imbalance, and aberrant reactive oxygen species production, contributes to persistent inflammation and disease pathogenesis. Among emerging mitochondrial immunometabolic regulators, the IRG1/ACOD1-derived metabolite itaconate has gained attention as a critical molecular integrator linking mitochondrial metabolism to inflammatory control.
This review systematically summarizes the biosynthesis of itaconate and its role in mitochondrial metabolic remodeling during inflammation. Itaconate reshapes the tricarboxylic acid cycle and inhibits succinate dehydrogenase, thereby limiting mitochondrial reactive oxygen species generation and preventing amplification of pro-inflammatory signaling. Through covalent modification of KEAP1, it activates the NRF2 antioxidant program, while concurrently restraining NLRP3 inflammasome activation, establishing a mitochondrial metabolic checkpoint that constrains excessive immune activation. Beyond acute metabolic regulation, itaconate coordinates sustained immunoregulatory programs via the ATF3-IκBζ transcriptional axis, autophagy-lysosome system modulation, and epigenetic reprogramming. We further integrate cell-type-specific effects of itaconate across macrophages, dendritic cells, T cells, and neutrophils, and discuss how mitochondrial immunometabolic dysregulation contributes to chronic inflammatory and metabolic disorders.
By positioning the IRG1-itaconate axis within the broader framework of mitochondrial immunometabolism, this review highlights mitochondria as a central hub linking metabolic remodeling with inflammatory regulation. Targeting mitochondrial metabolic checkpoints such as the itaconate pathway may provide promising therapeutic strategies for restoring immune homeostasis and treating inflammation-associated diseases.

v6.resumo: Revisão do itaconato como nó de imunometabolismo e controle inflamatório. 💡 Checar se a via de IRG1/itaconato tem ortólogo em Aedes e se aparece nos dados de metabolismo da linhagem Aag2.

articles.titulo: NADPH phosphatase activity of Mesh1 contributes to sleep regulation in Drosophila.
articles.autores: Ishikawa T, Nitta Y, … Masuda S (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Metazoans possess Mesh1, an enzyme with both ppGpp hydrolase and NADPH phosphatase activities, raising questions about their respective physiological roles. To distinguish these functions, we combined biochemical characterization, structure-guided mutagenesis, genome editing, and behavioral analysis in Drosophila. We found that Drosophila Mesh1 dephosphorylates NADPH but not NADP+ in vitro. Substitution of tryptophan 138 with phenylalanine (W138F) abolished detectable NADPH phosphatase activity while retaining detectable but severely reduced ppGpp hydrolase activity. Flies carrying the W138F mutation exhibited reduced total sleep duration and increased sleep fragmentation. These findings implicate the NADPH phosphatase activity of Mesh1 in sleep regulation and identify W138 as a critical residue for this function. Our results highlight a physiological role for Mesh1 beyond ppGpp metabolism and suggest a connection between NADPH metabolism and the regulation of sleep in metazoans.

v6.resumo: 🎲 [exploração] A atividade de NADPH fosfatase de Mesh1 (resíduo W138) regula sono em Drosophila. 💡 NADPH é substrato de ROS imune; a perna metabólica fica como hipótese para imunometabolismo de inseto.

articles.titulo: Microbes and diet reshape the Drosophila intestine via distinct cellular dynamics.
articles.autores: Bonfini A, Buchon N (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The intestine adapts to environmental challenges by changing size, but whether such remodeling reflects fixed homeostatic restoration or context-dependent adaptation remains unclear. Here, using Drosophila melanogaster, we combine defined diets with oral bacterial infection to quantify midgut size, cell number, cell size, and epithelial turnover. We show that diet and infection reshape the midgut through distinct cellular programs. Infection causes rapid shrinkage only when the organ was initially large, whereas post-infection regrowth requires dietary nutrients and converges toward a diet-defined state rather than a fixed pre-injury size. Diet-driven expansion occurs primarily through enterocyte hypertrophy and persists after stem cell ablation, whereas infection-induced recovery requires intestinal stem cell/progenitor activity. Microbes also have context-dependent effects, acting as damaging stressors in nutrient-rich conditions but promoting growth and survival under nutrient-poor conditions. These findings reveal modular cellular strategies through which diet and microbes jointly shape epithelial plasticity.

articles.titulo: Clock misalignment, not structural loss, underlies memory impairment following disruption of the mushroom body.
articles.autores: Dissel S, Tan WJ, … Shaw PJ (23 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The Drosophila mushroom body (MB) is a central circuit for many forms of associative learning, including olfactory conditioning, courtship conditioning, and aversive phototaxic suppression (APS). Kenyon cells (KCs), the intrinsic neurons of the MB, can be severely disrupted but not entirely eliminated by hydroxy urea (HU) treatment during development. Here, we show that HU-treated flies are profoundly impaired in short- and long-term memory under baseline conditions and that enhanced sleep restores learning in these animals. We establish the robustness of this finding using multiple behavioral assays and two independent methods to enhance sleep. Mechanistic analyses reveal that HU treatment disrupts circadian clock output, mistiming activity in γ-lobe-projecting dopaminergic neurons (DANs) and MB output neurons (MBONs). We further show that this mistiming is mediated, in part, by pigment-dispersing factor (PDF) signaling onto γ2-projecting DANs. Enhanced sleep restores the proper temporal coordination of these circuits. Strikingly, selectively reducing PDF receptor (Pdfr) signaling in these DANs also restored memory in HU-treated flies despite markedly reduced sleep, demonstrating that correcting mistimed clock signals can reproduce the restorative effects of sleep. These findings indicate that memory impairments after HU treatment can arise from disrupted temporal coordination within the MB circuit and demonstrate that downstream MBON-DAN interactions can support learning when properly regulated.

v6.resumo: Perda do corpo cogumelar de Drosophila por hidroxiureia prejudica memória por desalinhamento do relógio (via PDF/Pdfr em neurônios dopaminérgicos), não por perda estrutural; restaurar sono ou reduzir Pdfr corrige. Sem ligação direta com mosquito; interessa como lógica de temporização circadiana em circuito de aprendizado.

articles.titulo: Co-translational surveillance of nascent polypeptides times circadian rhythms in Drosophila.
articles.revista: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
articles.autores: Geisseova TK, Lee H, … Lee J (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Ribosome-associated quality control (RQC) ensures proteostasis by actively degrading aberrant translation intermediates on stalled ribosomes, yet its physiological role in gene regulation remains elusive. Here, we demonstrate that Drosophila circadian clocks employ RQC to sustain 24-h behavioral rhythms. RNA interference-mediated depletion of RQC components in circadian pacemaker neurons impaired free-running locomotor rhythms. In particular, the loss of Caliban (Clbn) function in clearing 60S-associated faulty polypeptides led to weak but long-period rhythms in adult locomotor activity. These behavioral phenotypes were accompanied by delayed accumulation of the core clock protein PERIOD (PER), most evidently in pigment-dispersing factor-expressing clock neurons, and dampened structural plasticity of their axons. per heterozygosity exaggerated CLBN depletion-induced period lengthening, whereas overexpression of the PER-associating factor TIMELESS blunted this effect. Clbn deficiency in Drosophila S2R+ cell cultures increased the generation of prematurely terminated PER species, particularly when PER translation is high, and sensitized full-length PER to phosphorylation-dependent decay. These findings support PER as a clock-relevant RQC substrate, providing a mechanistic link between translation flux, co-translational surveillance, and circadian timekeeping.

v6.resumo: Controle de qualidade de ribossomo (RQC, Caliban) sustenta ritmos circadianos em Drosophila: sem Clbn, PERIOD acumula atrasado e o período alonga; TIMELESS atenua o efeito. Lido junto ao Cell sobre timeless em An. stephensi, aponta que o par PER/TIM é ponto de ajuste de fisiologia em inseto.

articles.titulo: MitoEM 2.0: A Benchmark for Challenging 3D Mitochondria Instance Segmentation from EM Images.
articles.autores: Liu P, Shen B, … Wei D (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: We present MitoEM 2.0, a difficulty-aware extension of the original MitoEM benchmark for training and evaluating three-dimensional (3D) mitochondria instance segmentation in volume electron microscopy. The collection assembles multiscale vEM datasets (FIB-SEM, SBF-SEM, ssSEM) spanning diverse tissues and species, with expert-verified instance labels emphasizing biologically difficult scenarios, including dense mitochondrial packing, hyperfused networks, and thin filamentous connections with ambiguous boundaries. All releases include native-resolution volumes and standardized processed versions, per-volume metadata (voxel size, modality, tissue, splits), and official train/validation/test partitions to enable reproducible benchmarking. Annotations follow a consistent protocol with quality checks and instance reindexing. Data are provided in NIfTI with nnU-Net-compatible layout and OME-Zarr for cloud-aware workflows, alongside machine-readable split files and checksums. Baseline scripts support common training pipelines and size-stratified evaluation. By consolidating challenging volumes and harmonized labels, MitoEM 2.0 facilitates robust model development and fair comparison across methods while supporting reuse in bioimage analysis, algorithm benchmarking, and teaching.

v6.resumo: MitoEM 2.0: benchmark de segmentação 3D de instâncias de mitocôndrias em microscopia eletrônica de volume (FIB-SEM, SBF-SEM, ssSEM) com rótulos verificados, formatos nnU-Net e OME-Zarr e scripts de base. Relevante para a análise da MET de volume da glândula salivar de Anopheles.
v6.metodo: Scripts de treino e avaliação estratificada por tamanho, disponíveis no benchmark.

articles.titulo: Antimalarial activity of Croton caudatus Geiseler leaf extract and its ability to reduce experimental cerebral malaria pathogenesis.
articles.autores: Chatterjee A, Singh N, … Nagaraj VA (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Croton caudatus Geiseler is widely used in traditional medicine to treat various ailments, including malaria. However, scientific evidences supporting its antimalarial activity and the associated molecular mechanisms, and its potential to reduce severe malaria complications are lacking.
The present study was aimed to evaluate the antimalarial activity of C. caudatus leaf extract and its fractions, and to investigate the underlying molecular mechanisms.
Methanolic leaf extract of C. caudatus (CcLE) was fractionated into water (CcWater), butanol (CcBut), chloroform (CcChl), and hexane (CcHex) fractions. In vitro antiplasmodial activity was assessed against two different strains of Plasmodium falciparum (Pf): Pf3D7 and PfCam3.IR539T, alongside cytotoxicity and hemolysis assays. Phytochemical profiling of the most active fraction was performed by chemical fingerprinting. Mechanistic studies included β-hematin polymerization inhibition, hemozoin quantification, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) measurement. Acute oral toxicity and in vivo antimalarial efficacy were carried out in Plasmodium berghei (Pb) ANKA-infected BALB/c mice. Experimental cerebral malaria (ECM) studies were performed in Pb ANKA-infected C57BL/6 mice through the assessment of blood-brain barrier integrity, inflammatory marker expression, and immune cell infiltration analyses. Examining the gametocyte numbers and ex vivo exflagellation assays were carried out with Pb ANKA-infected mouse blood to assess the gametocytocidal activity.
CcHex exhibited the highest antiplasmodial activity against Pf 3D7 (IC50 = 6.84 ± 0.61 μg/mL) without detectable cytotoxic or hemolytic effects. Phytochemical analysis suggested the presence of bioactive metabolites associated with antimalarial activity. CcHex inhibited β-hematin formation in a cell-free assay and reduced hemozoin levels in Pf3D7 parasites, supporting its potential to interfere with parasite heme detoxification. It also increased intracellular ROS levels in the parasites, suggesting the disruption of heme detoxification. Further, CcHex treatment reduced gametocyte formation and impaired male gametocyte exflagellation, indicating gametocytocidal activity. Acute toxicity studies demonstrated a favourable safety profile. In Pb-infected Balb/c mice, CcHex treatment produced ∼62% parasite suppression at 1000 mg/kg/day. Importantly, CcHex treatment could protect against ECM by preserving blood-brain barrier integrity, and significantly reducing the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α and IFN-γ), chemokines (CXCL9, CXCL10, and CXCR3), the adhesion molecule ICAM-1, and CD8+ T-cell infiltration in the brain.
The present study demonstrates that C. caudatus, a traditionally used medicinal plant, possesses significant antiplasmodial activity, exhibits protective effects against ECM, and impairs male gametocyte exflagellation. CcHex showed potent antimalarial efficacy through inhibition of parasite heme detoxification, induction of oxidative stress, and modulation of host inflammatory responses. These results support the ethnopharmacological use of C. caudatus and highlight its potential as a source of bioactive phytochemicals for the development of novel antimalarials and adjunctive therapies against severe malaria.

v6.resumo: Extrato de folha de Croton caudatus: atividade contra P. falciparum 3D7 (CI50 6,84 µg/mL da fração hexano), inibição de β-hematina, efeito gametocitocida e, em P. berghei ANKA, preservação da barreira hematoencefálica e menos infiltração imune no modelo de malária cerebral experimental. Mecanismo é de heme/ROS; interessa pelo painel de ECM (integridade de BHE e infiltrado) como referência de leitura.

articles.titulo: Spatio-Temporal Modeling of Malaria Occurrence Probability Using Multi-Sensor Remote Sensing and Machine Learning.
articles.autores: Hassanpour G, Youssefi F, … Hanafi-Bojd AA (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Reliable mapping of malaria occurrence requires validation across environmentally distinct years and careful separation of model-derived probability from transmission intensity. This study developed a multi-sensor remote sensing and machine-learning framework for mapping annual malaria case occurrence in southeastern Iran.
Annual median composites of Soil Water Index (SWI), Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and Land Surface Temperature (LST) were generated from Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8/9 at 30m resolution. After quality control, 82, 168, 775 and 483 malaria case locations were retained for the Solar Hijri years 1400-1403 (2021-2025). Five spatially balanced pseudo-absence realizations were generated annually at a 1:1 ratio with a 300m exclusion buffer. Random Forest (RF) and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) were evaluated through complete four-fold leave-one-year-out validation with nested tuning. Performance, bootstrap confidence intervals, uncertainty, Getis-Ord Gi* clusters and SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) were assessed.
Across 20 outer evaluations, RF achieved ROC-AUC 0.685±0.045, PR-AUC 0.693±0.040, balanced accuracy 0.624±0.026 and Brier score 0.230±0.015. XGBoost achieved ROC-AUC 0.687±0.044, PR-AUC 0.691±0.043, balanced accuracy 0.625±0.033 and Brier score 0.231±0.015. Year-specific ROC-AUC ranged from 0.624 to 0.726. LST was the dominant predictor (48.27%), followed by NDVI (37.04%) and SWI (14.69%). Only 3.46-6.10% of pixels exceeded probability 0.70. Mean uncertainty was low (0.030-0.032) but spatially heterogeneous.
Both algorithms showed moderate, comparable performance with year-dependent variation. Maps provide relative probabilities for prioritizing field surveillance, not transmission estimates.

v6.resumo: Modelagem espaço-temporal da probabilidade de malária com sensoriamento remoto multissensor e aprendizado de máquina.

articles.titulo: Integrating Local Occurrence Records and Monthly Spatiotemporal Thermal Analysis to Predict Current and Future High-Risk Areas of Aedes albopictus in Guilan Province, Iran.
articles.autores: Karimi S, Jamshidi E, … Hanafi-Bojd AA (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Aedes albopictus, a key vector of arboviral diseases, has already been detected in Guilan Province, Iran, and is emerging as a public health concern in the country. This study aimed to identify monthly high-risk areas of Ae. albopictus and predict its distribution in Guilan Province using ecological niche modeling under current and projected climate scenarios. Guilan Province, with its high annual influx of travellers and active maritime ports, represents a strategic area for monitoring Ae. albopictus establishment.
A total of 200 occurrence points were obtained from local entomological surveys and health authorities. Four MaxEnt models were developed: current baseline (bioclimatic variables + elevation); current enhanced (bioclimatic variables + elevation + LST, NDVI, NDWI and population); and two future scenarios (SSP1-2.6 and SSP5-8.5, year 2030, CMIP6). Model performance was excellent, with AUC values of 0.909 and 0.908 for the baseline and enhanced models, respectively. articles.titulo: Neighborhood-scale modeling of Culex tarsalis abundance and West Nile virus infection prevalence.
articles.autores: Wong TS, Brooks W, … Barker CM (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Prevention of West Nile virus (WNV) transmission relies heavily on vector surveillance and control. Current methods of population reduction are often reactive, guided by field surveillance. Vector control measures would benefit from neighborhood-scale, spatiotemporal predictions of WNV risk that could facilitate proactive, targeted surveillance to locations and times where vector and virus activity is expected to be highest. To determine the potential of predictions at this spatial scale, we approached model development in two phases: (1) inferential generalized additive models were developed using high-density mosquito data collected across Davis, CA that identified causal associations between neighborhood-scale spatial features and relative abundance or WNV infection prevalence in Culex tarsalis; (2) Bayesian predictive models for Cx. tarsalis abundance and WNV prevalence were constructed by incorporating neighborhood-scale spatial variables with temporal and climatic predictors, using historical vector surveillance data from Davis between 2006 - 2024. Final predictive models included terms for spatial, meteorologic, and temporal variables, and performed well for Cx. tarsalis abundance and WNV prevalence when challenged with novel data from Davis or the neighboring town of Woodland, CA. articles.titulo: Early detection of dengue outbreaks from routine primary health care records: evaluation by an extended version of the Mixed Model of Artificial Intelligence and Next-Generation (MMAING).
articles.autores: Borges DGF, Coutinho ER, … Andrade RFS (13 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
A recently proposed surveillance framework is used to detect arbovirus outbreaks. It mixes traditional compartmental models with artificial intelligence techniques applied to large volumes of unconventional data on syndromic events, environment, and social information, and its performance is evaluated in the early identification of dengue epidemic events in Brazil at municipal level.
We evaluated an extended version of the MMAING model, referred to as MMAING-Arbo, developed to enable the early detection of dengue outbreaks based on primary health care (PHC) encounters associated with specific arboviral syndromes at the municipal level in Brazil. These findings reinforce the importance that future surveillance systems include data-driven approaches that benefit from the integration of multiple models, strengthening sensitivity, specificity, and timeliness of EWS.

articles.titulo: Semi-field efficacy of conspecific egg- and larva-derived chemical cues for manipulating Aedes aegypti oviposition.

Conspecific immature stages are known to influence oviposition-site selection and several egg and/or larvae derived compounds have been identified as potential oviposition cues under laboratory conditions. However, their performance under field conditions remains poorly understood, limiting their application in baited mass-trapping strategies. Using two-choice oviposition assays in outdoor cages, we evaluated under semi-field conditions the efficacy of five Ae. aegypti eggs and/or larvae associated compounds to influence oviposition in this mosquito species: (Z)-5-dodecenoic acid, pentadecanoic acid, n-heneicosane, palmitoleic acid and dodecanoic acid. An infusion of Ae. aegypti larvae was also tested under these conditions as positive control. We identified (Z)-5-dodecenoic acid as a potential volatile oviposition mediator, showing a trend toward increased oviposition (57 % of eggs received; oviposition attractivity index (OAI) = 0.14). For this compound, sticky-screen assays showed significant attraction compared to the control, excluding its detection by contact cues and suggesting its potential spatial activity to attract mosquitoes (attractivity index = 0.45). In contrast, n-heneicosane, and dodecanoic acid induced neutral oviposition responses (OAI = -0.03 and -0.1, respectively), whereas pentadecanoic and palmitoleic acids induced a trend toward slight oviposition deterrence in our settings (OAI = -0.17 and -0.20, respectively). Although previous laboratory or field evidence supporting their efficiency, our results reveal marked discrepancies between laboratory and semi-field behavioral responses. These findings emphasize the need for semi-field and field trials to assess mosquito semiochemicals, where long-range attraction can be distinguished from short-range oviposition stimulation, before considering their operational use in vector surveillance and control.

articles.titulo: Insecticide Resistance Dynamics in Aedes aegypti (Diptera: Culicidae) from Different Habitats in the Punjab, Pakistan.
articles.autores: Hayat M, Nasir S, … Sultana S (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
The mosquito Aedes aegypti is the most important vector of many viral diseases, such as dengue virus. Thus, various chemical insecticides are being used to control this vector. On the other hand, due to the intensive blind use of chemical insecticides, mosquito vectors are rapidly developing resistance against most of them.
The present study was conducted during 2024-25 to explore the development of resistance in three Ae. aegypti strains with a previous history of insecticidal records compared with Laboratory (LAB) and Tidiwala (TDW) strains collected from localities (Tidiwala and rural barren land) with no or minimal use of insecticides. Resistance development was recorded by utilizing five commonly used insecticides against mosquitoes in Punjab, Pakistan.
Results showed that deltamethrin was the best during 2024 when compared with alpha-cypermethrin, temephos, lambda-cyhalothrin and Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis. All field-collected strains revealed significant resistance to the tested insecticides compared with LAB and TDW strains. The same findings were reflected in the enzyme spectrum (glutathione-S-transferase, mixed-function oxidases, esterase, and acetylcholinesterase).
These results may help to devise a comprehensive future strategy for mosquito control through selective insecticides by limiting the spread of resistance.

articles.titulo: Evolutionarily distinct dengue virus type 2 with a unique type-specific neutralization determinant.
articles.revista: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
articles.autores: Mayer SV, Winkelmann ER, … Katzelnick LC (16 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Dengue viruses 1-4 (DENV1-4) mostly circulate in endemic cycles involving humans and Aedes mosquitoes. However, rare dengue outbreaks originate from non-human primates. These spillovers are caused by sylvatic virus genotypes that are closely related to endemic strains of the same serotype, but some are caused by strains that fall between the four canonical serotypes on phylogenetic trees. It is not clear whether these genotypic differences are reflected in corresponding antigenic differences. Here, we characterized the antigenic features of QML-22, a divergent strain most closely related to DENV2. On an antigenic map, QML-22 clustered with other globally representative DENV2 strains. QML-22 was not as well neutralized by antisera raised against endemic DENV2 and was better neutralized by antisera from DENV1, 3, and 4 infections than other strains of DENV2. QML-22 had a cluster of distinct amino acid residues in domain I of the envelope (E) protein, with only scattered point mutations elsewhere in the envelope. A potently neutralizing anti-DENV2 antibody that targets this site in domain I of the E protein, 3F9, had >1000-fold lower neutralization of QML-22 than other endemic DENV2 strains, whereas other cross-reactive and DENV2-specific antibodies neutralized QML-22 and endemic strains to similar titers. When antisera from non-human primates infected with QML-22 or DENV2 reference strain S16803 were depleted with the heterologous virions, homologous neutralization was unaffected but heterologous neutralization was reduced, suggesting homologous neutralization was due to distinct epitopes. Evolutionary analyses showed the 3F9 epitope was under relaxed selection pressure compared to other neutralizing epitopes and that QML-22 had unique amino acids in this epitope relative to the likely common ancestor of all DENV2. These findings provide insight into the antigenic diversification of DENV and the possible evolution of new serotypes.
Dengue viruses that are most distantly related to the four canonical serotypes originated in Borneo, suggesting this island is a possible site of early dengue virus diversification as well as continued evolution within an unidentified host species. Here, we find divergent strain QML-22 from Borneo shares many neutralizing epitopes with DENV2 but has a distinct epitope in an important region affecting potent DENV2 neutralization. This region of the virus also is variable within DENV2 and in other DENV serotypes, highlighting an important site of dengue virus diversification and evolution. The spillover threat of viruses like QML-22 remains unknown, but ecological changes in Borneo may increase this risk.

articles.titulo: Bacterial and fungal diversity in Anopheles larval habitats with different productivities.
articles.autores: Forson AO, Afrane YA, … Hurwitz I (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Anopheles gambiae mosquitoes develop in diverse aquatic habitats, where microbial communities influence oviposition, larval growth, and survival. This study characterized bacterial and fungal communities across Anopheles larval habitats of differing productivity in southern Ghana.
Larval densities were monitored bi-weekly over 6 months. Water and larval samples were collected for bacterial (16S rRNA gene) and fungal (ITS) amplicon sequencing. Based on the consistency of Anopheles larval presence throughout the monitoring period, habitats were classified as high-productive (larvae present at every visit), low-productive (intermittent larval presence), or non-productive (larvae consistently absent).
The study revealed that distinct microbial signatures were associated with habitat productivity. Linear discriminant analysis identified Paraclostridium bifermentans and Bacillus spp. as indicator taxa for high-productive habitats, while Acinetobacter variabilis and Lactococcus garvieae were associated with low-productive habitats. For fungi, Cladosporium halotolerans and Aspergillus penicillioides were the primary discriminant taxa associated with high-productive habitats, while Candida tropicalis and Pichia kudriavzevii characterized low-productive habitats. Beta-diversity analyses revealed significant differences in bacterial communities between productive and non-productive habitats (PERMANOVA, p = 0.006), whereas fungal communities showed no significant separation.
These findings highlight an association between microbial assemblages and larval-habitat suitability and underscore the potential of microbiota-informed strategies to enhance vector surveillance and targeted larval control.

articles.titulo: Dynamics of Drosophila immune stress hematopoiesis assessed by single cell transcriptomics.
articles.autores: Morin-Poulard I, Liu X, … Crozatier M (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The molecular complexity of the hematopoietic microenvironment (niche) and its response to immune stress remain largely unknown. Here, we establish the transcriptional profile of the lymph gland, the Drosophila hematopoietic organ, and its associated niche, the posterior signaling center, at single-cell resolution and at different time points following an immune challenge. Among blood cells, we identify permanent cellular states present with and without stress, but also transient states specific to the immune response, which correspond to dividing cells primed to differentiate into dedicated effector cells. The niche itself is a heterogeneous cell population, and most niche cells undergo dynamic transcriptional remodeling following immune stress. Finally, we identify two new players involved in the hematopoietic stress response: the immune deficiency pathway and the cholecystokinin-like receptor, both of which are expressed in niche cell subsets during immune stress conditions. This molecular atlas of lymph gland cells at different time points after an immune challenge provides new insights into the control of stress hematopoiesis by discrete niche cell subsets.

articles.titulo: Elevated serum levels of interferon-stimulated gene 15 are associated with the prevalence of hypertriglyceridemia.
articles.revista: Clinica chimica acta; international journal of clinical chemistry
articles.autores: Zheng X, Xiang Q, … Xu J (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Hypertriglyceridemia (HTG) is a prevalent dyslipidemia worldwide and an independent risk factor for cardiovascular disease and acute pancreatitis. Interferon-stimulated gene 15 (ISG15), a ubiquitin-like protein involved in innate immunity, has recently been implicated in metabolic disorders, but its relationship with HTG remains unexplored.
This study included 295 Chinese participants (184 with HTG and 111 without HTG). Serum ISG15 levels were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, and associations with HTG were assessed using logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Findings were validated in high-fat diet (HFD)-induced HTG mouse through western blotting, immunohistochemistry, and histological analyses.
Serum ISG15 levels were significantly elevated in HTG patients compared with controls (3.18 ± 0.29 vs. 1.64 ± 0.19, P < 0.001). Multivariate logistic regression identified ISG15 as an independent predictor of HTG (OR: 1.214, 95% CI: 1.015-1.416, P = 0.033). RCS analysis revealed a nonlinear dose-response relationship with an inflection point at approximately 1.52 ng/mL. ROC analysis demonstrated good diagnostic performance (AUC: 0.697, sensitivity: 86.40%, specificity: 45.00% at cut-off 0.873 ng/mL). In HFD-fed mice, serum ISG15 levels were significantly elevated, and immunohistochemistry and western blotting confirmed increased ISG15 expression in liver, subcutaneous white adipose tissue, and epididymal white adipose tissue.
ISG15 is independently associated with HTG and exhibits a nonlinear relationship with diagnostic potential. These findings establish ISG15 as a potential biomarker and suggest its involvement in the immunometabolic crosstalk underlying HTG pathogenesis, warranting further mechanistic investigation.

articles.titulo: Mapping the Three-Dimensional Chromatin Structure of the Harpegnathos saltator Brain by Micro-C.
articles.autores: Kuang M, Shields EJ, … Bonasio R (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The socially inducible brain and behavioral reprogramming observed in the ant Harpegnathos saltator provides a unique opportunity for investigating how three-dimensional (3D) chromatin architecture, organized across multiple spatial scales, shapes (or is shaped by) gene regulation and adult brain plasticity. Micro-C, a chromatin conformation capture technique, enables genome-wide detection of chromatin interactions at single-nucleosome resolution. Applying Micro-C to challenging or low-input samples, such as the brain of a single adult insect with a specific behavioral phenotype, however, poses significant technical obstacles. Here, we describe an optimized Micro-C protocol for obtaining 3D chromatin contact maps from the brain of a single Harpegnathos ant. The protocol successfully enables the definition of large-scale folding patterns, such as A/B compartments and topologically associating domains (TADs), as well as the detailed interrogation of fine-scale enhancer-promoter loops in the brain. This protocol thus expands the accessibility of Micro-C to brains or other organs in these organisms, allowing the investigation of species- and caste-specific features of chromatin architecture in social insect brains and beyond.

articles.titulo: Regulation of sociality and neuronal development by the translation initiation factor eIF4H1 in Drosophila.
articles.revista: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
articles.autores: Nolan E, Chin I, … Ben-Shahar Y (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Most animal species exhibit some level of sociality. However, whether sociality-related traits evolved independently, or are instead derived from common core mechanisms, remains controversial. Nevertheless, an emerging theoretical framework stipulates that key aspects of how animals interact with their social environments may be regulated by a phylogenetically conserved genetic toolkit. Therefore, we hypothesized that mutations that lead to social deficits in specific human disorders may implicate genes that play conserved roles in the regulation of core social traits across Animalia. Specifically, here we focus on genes associated with Williams syndrome (WS), a rare human multi-system disorder characterized in part by hypersocial cognitive traits. WS is caused by a hemizygous chromosomal microdeletion of 25-28 protein-coding genes. Consequently, it has been hypothesized that haploinsufficiency in at least one of these genes plays an important role in the development and/or function of social neural circuits in humans. Because the Drosophila genome encodes orthologs of 17 of the 28 genes deleted in WS, we reasoned that at least some of them may serve a conserved role in the regulation of social traits across flies and humans, as predicted by the genetic toolkit framework. Using a neuron-specific RNAi knockdown screen, we identified eIF4H1 , an ortholog of a highly conserved subunit of the eukaryotic translation initiation complex eIF4F, as a candidate gene for neuronal regulation of sociality in the fly. We show that eIF4H1 expression is predominantly neuronal in the adult fly brain, and that its action plays a differential role in the organization of specific dopaminergic neuron subtypes that are associated with sociality and cognitive functions. These results indicate that eIF4H1 may serve a conserved function in regulating the development of the neuronal circuits that regulate social behaviors, thus supporting the idea of a conserved sociality genetic toolkit.

articles.titulo: Engineered microorganisms drive local metabolic reprogramming to Re-educate systemic immunity.
articles.autores: Ma Y, Yang Y, … Li Z (14 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) features chronic synovial inflammation and systemic immune disorders. Current treatments mainly rely on systemic immunosuppression, raising risks of infection and long-term immune injury. Local therapies reduce such risks but struggle to regulate systemic immunity. Emerging studies show the synovial immunometabolic microenvironment links local inflammation to systemic responses. Here, we developed a strategy based on chemically attenuated photosynthetic bacteria that couples lactate metabolism with photo-driven hydrogen production to achieve local metabolic reprogramming and systemic immune re-education. We screened a photosynthetic bacterial strain with high lactate metabolic capacity, which also exhibited enhanced hydrogen production. To ensure safety, bacteria were PEGylated to mask immunogenic moieties while preserving metabolic activity. Intra-articular injection disrupted pathological crosstalk and restored the Treg/Th17 balance locally. Circulating IL-6 levels decreased, restoring the systemic regulatory role of Tregs, thereby alleviating distant joint inflammation. These results demonstrate that local synovial metabolic reprogramming by engineered bacteria can induce systemic immune re-education, offering a conceptually new therapeutic strategy for treating autoimmune arthritis.

articles.titulo: Extracellular vesicles from human adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells reprogram macrophage lipid metabolism via the ABCF1/CPT1A/IL-10 axis to mitigate sepsis-induced acute lung injury.
articles.autores: Zhang L, Guo D, … Zhang S (15 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Sepsis-induced acute lung injury (ALI) is a life-threatening syndrome characterized by overwhelming inflammation, immune dysregulation, and tissue damage. Metabolic reprogramming of macrophages has emerged as a central regulator of inflammatory responses. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) offer therapeutic potential, but their molecular mechanisms in regulating immunometabolism during ALI remain unclear. Single-cell RNA sequencing (GSE207651) revealed enrichment of pro-inflammatory macrophages and activation of IL-1/TNF signaling in septic ALI. Human adipose-derived MSC-EVs (hADSC-EVs) were isolated and characterized by transmission electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking analysis, and Western blotting. Their effects on macrophage metabolism and polarization were assessed using bulk RNA-seq, Real-Time Quantitative Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-qPCR), Western blotting, flow cytometry, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), and lipid staining. In vivo efficacy was validated in a cecal ligation and puncture (CLP)-induced murine ALI model, and the macrophage-dependency of this therapy was confirmed using a genetic LysM-Cre; iDTR macrophage-ablation model. hADSC-EVs delivered ABCF1 into macrophages, upregulating CPT1A and IL-10, which is associated with fatty acid oxidation pathways, and promoting M2 polarization while suppressing NF-κB/STAT1-mediated inflammatory signaling. Silencing CPT1A disrupted lipid metabolism-associated profiles, reduced M2 polarization, and amplified pro-inflammatory responses. In vivo, hADSC-EVs alleviated pulmonary injury, decreased IL-1β and TNF-α release, and reduced apoptosis and inflammatory infiltration in lung tissue. ABCF1-deficient EVs lost these protective effects, highlighting the central role of the ABCF1/CPT1A/IL-10 axis. Collectively, our findings identify the ABCF1/CPT1A/IL-10 axis as a key immunometabolic pathway through which hADSC-EVs modulate macrophage lipid profiles to suppress inflammation, reduce apoptosis, and protect against sepsis-induced ALI. These results provide novel mechanistic insights into the interplay between metabolism, immune regulation, and cell death, highlighting EV-based strategies as promising therapeutic interventions for septic lung injury.
