articles.titulo: Phosphoric acid-functionalized biochar derived from residual neem seed biomass after biodiesel production for adsorption of brilliant green and malachite green dyes from contaminated water.
articles.autores: Sarker SC, Hossain MI, … Rahman MM (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: In this study, sorbents were produced and functionalized from the discarded residual biomass of the (Melia azadirachta) neem seeds (RMNSB) after biodiesel production. This biomass was selected because, during biodiesel production by transesterification and solvent washing operations, a huge amount of residual mass (∼80%) is generated, which is associated with secondary waste production. To achieve the zero-waste goal, the discarded biomass of neem seed was transformed into functionalized biochar, which has enhanced overall properties and sorption potential. The batch adsorption experiments for the simultaneous elimination of Brilliant Green (BG) and Malachite Green (MG) dyes from binary BG-MG solution wastewater were examined under varying parameters. Kinetic data demonstrated agreement with both the pseudo-first-order (R 2 > 0.99) and pseudo-second-order models (R 2 > 0.98) for the BG and MG dyes. Equilibrium data demonstrated good agreement with both the Langmuir (R 2 > 0.99) and Freundlich (R 2 > 0.99) isotherm models for the BG and MG dyes, which indicates the presence of simultaneous adsorption features depicted by both models. The specific surface area, sample density, pore volume, and pore diameter measured are approximately 49.5 m2 g-1, 1.00 g cm-3, 0.063 cm3 g-1, and 5.25 nm, respectively. Maximum adsorption capacity of BG and MG onto the bionanosorbent was recorded as 164.42 mg g-1 and 172.24 mg g-1, respectively. Analysis of other thermodynamic parameters confirmed the spontaneity and endothermic character of the adsorption of both dyes, with enhanced randomization at the interface between the bionanosorbent and solution. Further studies of the FRMNSB biochar samples were carried out utilizing Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy-Attenuated Total Reflectance (FTIR-ATR), Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy (FESEM), Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), Zeta Potential (ZP), and Simultaneous Thermal Analyzer (STA) analysis/techniques to provide a full understanding of the physicochemical, thermomechanical, and morpho-structural features.

articles.titulo: Uranium Removal and Integrated Physiological, Surface Chemical and Multi-omics Responses of Aspergillus niger under Uranium Exposure.
articles.autores: Han MW, Dong B, … Zhao SP (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Uranium contamination poses ecological and health risks, and fungi are promising candidates for radionuclide bioremediation because of their high biomass, extensive hyphal networks and abundant cell surface functional groups. In this study, a uranium-tolerant strain of Aspergillus niger isolated from biological soil crusts in a uranium tailings repository was used to investigate fungal responses to uranium exposure. Physiological and biochemical assays, microscopic observation, FTIR and XPS characterization, and multi-omics analyses, including transcriptomics, proteomics and intracellular metabolomics, were integrated to characterize its responses under different uranium exposure levels. After 7 d of cultivation, A. niger exhibited substantial uranium removal from the culture medium. The uranium removal efficiencies were 72.7%, 58.5%, and 80.9% in the U1 (10 mg/L), U2 (50 mg/L), and U3 (100 mg/L) treatments, respectively. Notably, removal efficiency did not increase monotonically with initial uranium concentration, with U3 showing the highest value. Antioxidant enzyme activities, including SOD, CAT and POD, together with GSH and GSSG contents, were altered under uranium exposure, indicating uranium-induced oxidative stress and antioxidant-related responses. FTIR and XPS analyses suggested that phosphate-, amide/carboxyl-, hydroxyl- and amino-related surface groups may participate in uranium association with the mycelial surface. Transcriptomic, proteomic and intracellular metabolomic analyses further revealed coordinated changes in carbon and energy metabolism, oxidative stress regulation, membrane transport-related proteins, phosphate metabolism-related proteins and intracellular organic acid-related metabolism. Notably, APase-related proteins may promote phosphate release and thereby facilitate phosphate-associated uranium immobilization, whereas ABC transporter-related proteins may contribute to membrane transport, efflux, and intracellular homeostasis under uranium stress. Overall, these candidate proteins suggest a mechanistic linkage between phosphate-mediated uranium immobilization and transporter-mediated uranium detoxification in A. niger, and provide prioritized molecular targets for future functional validation.

articles.titulo: Roxadustat ameliorates bone microarchitectural deterioration in CKD-MBD rats in association with mitigated systemic micro-inflammation and restored FGF23-Wnt/β-catenin signaling.
articles.autores: Shan Z, Liu Y, … Luo P (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Elevated FGF23 is associated with bone microarchitectural deterioration in chronic kidney dis-ease-mineral and bone disorder (CKD-MBD). While roxadustat (a HIF-PHI) is established for the treatment of renal anemia, its potential bone-protective effects in CKD-MBD remain unclear. We investigated whether roxadustat ameliorates femoral microarchitectural deterioration in CKD-MBD rats in association with FGF23 downregulation and restoration of Wnt/β-catenin signaling. A CKD-MBD rat model was established by unilateral nephrectomy and adenine gavage, and animals were randomized into sham, model, and roxadustat (50 or 100 mg/kg, three times weekly) groups for 8 weeks. Renal function, hematological indices, calcium-phosphate parame-ters, and femoral microarchitecture were evaluated, and target protein levels (FGF23, FGFR1, DKK1, β-catenin) were assessed by Western blotting and immunohistochemistry. Roxadustat improved renal function, ameliorated the reduction in erythroid parameters, and restored calcium-phosphate homeostasis. Systemically, it mitigated micro-inflammation by reducing serum CRP and hepcidin, and downregulated serum FGF23 levels as well as tissue FGF23 expression in kidney and bone. In conclusion, the bone-protective effect of roxadustat occurs synchronously with systemic micro-inflammation mitigation, FGF23 downregulation, and Wnt/β-catenin signaling restoration. These findings highlight its pleiotropic therapeutic potential in CKD-MBD management, suggesting a synergistic benefit associated with both systemic metabolic recovery and local skeletal regulation.

articles.titulo: Cutaneous Effects of Oral Polystyrene Microplastic Exposure in Mice: Oxidative Stress, Inflammation, and FGF5 Gene Dysregulation.
articles.autores: Islam MS, Koedrith P (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Microplastic (MP) pollution represents an escalating threat to mammalian health, yet the potential effects of oral MP exposure on mammalian skin remain poorly understood.
This study investigated the effects of oral polystyrene microplastic (PS-MP) exposure on skin integrity, oxidative balance, and the expression of the Fibroblast Growth Factor 5 (FGF5) gene a key regulator controlling the transition between hair growth and regression phases in the hair cycle.
Male Swiss albino mice were orally exposed to PS-MPs (4.8-5 µm) at low (0.1 mg) and high (0.2 mg) doses for 28 consecutive days. Biochemical analyses evaluated oxidative stress markers (CAT, SOD, POD, ROS, and MDA), serum enzyme activity (ALT, AST, ALP, and amylase), and mineral concentrations (Ca, Mg, and phosphate). Histopathological examination of H&E-stained skin sections assessed epidermal thickness, keratinocyte density, and dermal inflammation. Quantitative real-time PCR was used to measure FGF5 gene expression in dorsal skin, with Hprt1 as the internal control.
Oral PS-MP exposure was associated with dose-dependent oxidative stress in skin tissue, reflected by elevated ROS (0.545 → 1.99 U/mg) and MDA (1.49 → 7.37 nmol/L) levels and significant depletion of antioxidant enzymes such as CAT (10.2 → 4.33 U/mg protein). Serum biochemical disturbances confirmed systemic metabolic stress. Histopathology revealed epidermal hyperplasia (16.46 → 34.18 µm), reduced keratinocyte density (22.1 → 7.0), and marked inflammatory infiltration. Importantly, FGF5 expression increased 1.35-fold, suggesting altered regulation of pathways associated with hair-follicle cycling.
Oral PS-MP exposure was associated with oxidative stress, structural alterations, inflammation, and FGF5 upregulation in mouse skin. These findings suggest a potential association between oral PS-MP exposure and disruption of skin and hair-follicle homeostasis in mammals.

articles.titulo: Caste Transition, Behavioral Monitoring, and Tissue Harvesting in Harpegnathos saltator.
articles.autores: Moreno-Medina S, Kuang M, … Khan S (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Eusocial insects offer unique opportunities to investigate how epigenetic mechanisms shape brain function and plasticity, as distinct, fixed castes display different behavioral repertoires despite sharing the same genome. In the ant Harpegnathos saltator-unlike most eusocial insects-adult workers can transition into a queen-like reproductive state known as a gamergate. This ability to undergo reversible caste transitions makes Harpegnathos a powerful model for dissecting epigenetic regulation of neural and behavioral phenotypes. Accurate molecular profiling, however, relies on precise caste identification, careful brain isolation, and the verification of reproductive status through ovary dissection. Whereas dissection procedures are well established in model organisms such as Drosophila melanogaster, detailed protocols for eusocial insects are scarce, and are largely unavailable for Harpegnathos ants. Here, we describe protocols for studying caste transitions in Harpegnathos We provide step-by-step methods for inducing worker-gamergate caste transitions, monitoring and assigning individuals to the correct caste, and dissecting brains and ovaries. These protocols allow users to study various behavioral processes in ants and obtain high-quality tissue for downstream genomic and epigenomic applications aimed at uncovering the regulatory mechanisms underlying caste-specific phenotypes and development.

articles.titulo: Beyond antigens: TLR9-β-glucan nanocomplexes for 'X' respiratory viral infections.
articles.autores: Bonam SR, Prajapati A, Bayry J (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Pathogen-specific vaccines provide durable immunity, but the delayed rollout during emerging viral outbreaks leaves populations vulnerable. Tobuse et al. address this gap, demonstrating that intranasal administration of K3-SPG, an antigen-free, water-soluble β-glucan/Toll-like receptor 9 (TLR9)-agonist nanocomplex induces biphasic, tissue-restricted innate memory, conferring broad, antigen-independent protection against diverse respiratory viruses by limiting lung pathology.

articles.titulo: Exploratory colonic fermentation of lysozyme-hydrolyzed cricket exoskeleton in the TIM-2 in vitro model: descriptive microbiota and metabolite profiles compared with fructooligosaccharides.
articles.autores: Leetanasaksakul K, Visessanguan W, … Ruttarattanamongkol K (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Unlike conventional carbohydrate-based prebiotics, insect-derived byproducts deliver chitin alongside substantial residual protein, but the colonic fermentation of such multi-component substrates has received little attention. A lysozyme-hydrolyzed cricket exoskeleton product (LHCE) was prepared from the chitin-enriched residue remaining after pilot-scale protein extraction from house crickets (Acheta domesticus). On a dry-weight basis, LHCE contained 79.5 g/100 g crude protein (N × 6.25), 12.5 g/100 g crude fat, and 13.1 g/100 g gravimetrically recovered chitin; chitin represented a separate, non-additive empirical fraction. HPLC showed peaks co-eluting with N-acetylglucosamine monomer-to-tetramer standards, but their identities were not independently confirmed. LHCE and fructooligosaccharides (FOS) were fermented for 72 h in two independent TIM-2 vessels per substrate using aliquots of the same pooled donor microbiota. PacBio full-length 16S rRNA gene reads were processed with DADA2, yielding 317,680 nonchimeric reads and 1451 amplicon sequence variants across 16 samples. Bacillota and Bacteroidota dominated all vessels, while genus-level composition varied among vessels and over time. Microbiota and lumen/dialysate short-chain and branched-chain fatty acid profiles were evaluated descriptively because repeated measurements within vessels were not independent replicates. In LHCE vessels, lumen isobutyrate and isovalerate concentrations were higher at 24-72 h than at baseline. These patterns were compatible with branched-chain amino-acid metabolism but were insufficient to quantify fermentation rates or establish a broader proteolytic shift. Because baseline community profiles differed and the substrates were compositionally unmatched, observed differences could not be attributed specifically to chitin. These exploratory findings indicate feasibility; further studies require greater independent replication, composition-matched controls, and complete metabolite mass balances.

articles.titulo: Heartland Virus in Lone Star Ticks, South Carolina, USA, 2021-2024.
articles.autores: Pickle EO, Torelli MMM, … Nolan MS (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Tickborne arboviruses are a serious health threat, but surveillance gaps remain. We tested lone star nymphs collected in South Carolina, USA, for Heartland and Bourbon viruses. Six pools were positive for Heartland virus; none were positive for Bourbon virus. Longitudinal surveillance provides insights into the emergence and distribution of tickborne pathogens.

articles.titulo: Integrating Malaria Vaccine with Seasonal Malaria Chemoprevention in West Africa (IMVACS): study protocol for a cluster-randomized trial.
articles.autores: Natama HM, Ouoba S, … Tinto H (14 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Despite wide-scale implementation of malaria prevention strategies, including seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SMC), a substantial disease burden persists. The R21/Matrix-M (R21/MM) malaria vaccine, recommended by the World Health Organization in 2023, is expected to substantially reduce this burden in children. However, the optimal delivery strategy in highly seasonal transmission settings remains uncertain. Integrating vaccine delivery with SMC campaigns may improve access, timeliness, and coverage, especially for the fourth dose. This trial will evaluate whether integrated delivery of R21/MM through SMC campaigns will provide non-inferior protection against malaria compared with routine Essential Program on Immunization (EPI)-based delivery or routine pre-seasonal delivery before SMC campaigns. Feasibility, acceptability, and cost-effectiveness will also be assessed.
This trial is a multi-site, phase IV, open-label, two-arm, cluster-randomized, non-inferiority trial conducted in the rural health districts of Boussé (Burkina Faso) and Dioila (Mali). Clusters, defined as peripheral health centers catchment areas, will be randomized separately within each country (1:1) and stratified by cluster size, with 20 clusters in Burkina Faso and 16 in Mali. Following written informed consent, trained study staff will enroll eligible children. Children aged 3-59 months living in intervention clusters and those aged 5-36 months living in control clusters will be eligible for vaccination. Children with previous malaria vaccination or conditions compromising participation will be excluded. Vaccination will be delivered through integrated SMC campaigns in the intervention arm and through year-round EPI-based delivery in Burkina Faso or pre-seasonal delivery before SMC campaigns followed by year-round EPI-based delivery in Mali. Power calculations will assume a non-inferiority margin of 0.10. The primary outcome will be the incidence of clinical malaria among children aged 5-36 months over 12 months after the first dose. Secondary outcomes will include adverse events following immunization, adverse events of special interest, serious adverse events, vaccine coverage, dropout rates, barriers and facilitators to implementation, stakeholder perceptions, and cost per disability-adjusted life year averted.
Beyond effectiveness and safety, the study will provide evidence to support integrated R21/MM delivery with SMC in highly seasonal transmission settings. The findings are expected to inform national and global malaria vaccine policies.
ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06860178 . Registered on 20 January 2025.

articles.titulo: Bee Pollen-Derived Spermidine Derivative Improves d-Galactose-Induced Cognitive Impairment by Enhancing Cerebral Glutathione Redox Metabolism.
articles.autores: Deng S, Zhang Y, … Jiang Z (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Aging-related cognitive decline is closely associated with oxidative stress and gut microbiota dysbiosis. This study investigated the protective effects of di-p-coumaroyl-caffeoyl spermidine (SPDD) isolated from rose bee pollen in d-galactose-induced aging mice. Compared with the model group, SPDD significantly improved cognitive performance in the Y-maze, novel object recognition, and Morris water maze tests (p < 0.05). SPDD reduced MDA levels and restored SOD, CAT, and GSH-Px activities in serum, liver, and brain, while alleviating tissue and neuronal structural damage. Furthermore, SPDD reshaped gut microbiota composition by increasing Lactobacillus abundance and reducing Helicobacter abundance, accompanied by increased short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) production. Brain metabolomic and transcriptomic analyses indicated that SPDD activated glutathione metabolism. Molecular validation further showed that SPDD upregulated key targets in this pathway, including GCLC, GSR, and GPX4, suggesting enhanced GSH synthesis, regeneration, and peroxide clearance (p < 0.05). These findings indicate that the cognitive benefits of SPDD were associated with improved cerebral glutathione metabolism, whereas changes in gut microbiota composition and SCFA production occurred concurrently.

articles.titulo: Preclinical progress in the target validation of viroporins: candidates for potential target therapy.
articles.autores: Basu K, Arkin IT (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Numerous viral infections necessitate immediate attention, underscoring the urgent need for effective antiviral drugs that can directly inhibit viral functions or indirectly manipulate host factors. Most direct-acting antiviral drugs target two specific viral components: polymerases (including reverse transcriptases) and proteases. Focusing on this narrow range of targets limits the scope of drug development and favors rapid resistance emergence. Therefore, targeting alternative viral components, such as viroporins, is advantageous. Viroporins constitute a family of small hydrophobic proteins encoded by viruses that oligomerize to form ion channels, thereby playing crucial roles in various stages of the viral infectivity cycle. Despite their functional significance, they have received considerably less attention from the pharmaceutical industry compared to traditional viral targets.
This review delves into the significance of viral channels as potential therapeutic targets, surveying recent advancements and the prospects for future breakthroughs. Viroporins from diverse viral families and their potential inhibition by small molecules are discussed, with special emphasis on bacteria-based channel assays that facilitate high-throughput screening of channel blockers.
Bacteria-based assays enable rapid discovery and preemptive resistance mapping, while conserved pore architectures raise the prospect of broadspectrum inhibitors. However, clinical translation requires addressing selectivity, toxicity, and pharmacokinetic challenges.

articles.titulo: AGR3 drives M1 polarization and glycolytic reprogramming of pulmonary macrophages via stabilizing HIF-1α/PKM2 axis to aggravate CLP-induced sepsis-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome.
articles.autores: Zhou Y, Li W, Wang D (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Sepsis-associated acute respiratory distress syndrome (sepsis-ARDS) remains a life-threatening critical illness with limited targeted therapeutics, where pulmonary macrophage M1 polarization and aerobic glycolysis act as core drivers of inflammatory lung injury. Anterior gradient 3 (AGR3), an endoplasmic reticulum disulfide isomerase, was recently identified as a dysregulated transcript in human ARDS patient datasets, yet its immunometabolic function in septic lung injury remains undefined. Here, we aimed to characterize the role and molecular cascade of AGR3 in regulating macrophage polarization and glycolytic reprogramming during polymicrobial sepsis, combining the in vivo CLP septic mouse model with an in vitro LPS/IFN-γ-induced M1 polarization model in RAW264.7 macrophages. Bioinformatic mining of GSE66890 RNA-seq dataset revealed prominent AGR3 upregulation in human ARDS lung tissues, which we validated in cecal ligation and puncture (CLP)-induced septic mouse lungs and LPS/IFN-γ-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages. Lentiviral-mediated AGR3 knockdown suppressed M1 macrophage polarization, reduced glycolytic flux (lower ECAR, higher OCR, diminished lactate secretion), and blunted pro-inflammatory cytokine release in vitro. Mechanistic biochemistry assays demonstrated that AGR3 physically interacts with hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α), extending HIF-1α protein half-life by restraining proteasomal degradation and promoting its nuclear translocation. Chromatin immunoprecipitation confirmed that stabilized nuclear HIF-1α transcriptionally activates pyruvate kinase M2 (Pkm2), a master glycolytic effector. Reciprocal rescue experiments verified that ectopic overexpression of HIF-1α or PKM2 largely reversed the anti-inflammatory, metabolic phenotypes induced by AGR3 silencing. In vivo intratracheal AAV9-shAGR3 delivery mitigated CLP-triggered pulmonary edema, neutrophil infiltration, M1 macrophage accumulation, and restored protective PKM2 tetramer formation, accompanied by significant improvement in pulmonary function and 7-day survival of septic mice. Taken together, AGR3 mediates sepsis-induced lung injury via the HIF-1α/PKM2 signaling. This study provides a novel potential therapeutic target for sepsis-associated ARDS.

articles.titulo: Machine learning identifies mitochondria-related biomarkers for Staphylococcus aureus osteomyelitis with validation in mouse and human bone tissues.
articles.revista: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
articles.autores: Deng X, Yang F, … Ao J (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Staphylococcus aureus (SA)-induced osteomyelitis (OM) is a severe orthopedic infection characterized by complex host-pathogen interactions and limited molecular markers for lesion assessment. Mitochondrial dysfunction is closely linked to infection-induced inflammatory and metabolic remodeling, but mitochondria-related signatures in SA-induced OM remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to identify mitochondria-related candidate biomarkers for SA-induced OM and evaluate their associations with immune infiltration and regulated cell death.
Peripheral-blood transcriptomic datasets GSE16129 and GSE6269 were used as the training cohort, and whole-blood dataset GSE30119 was used as an external evaluation cohort. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified using limma and intersected with MitoCarta3.0 to obtain mitochondria-related DEGs (MRDEGs). GO and KEGG enrichment analyses were performed. Core MRDEGs were selected using LASSO, SVM-RFE, and Random Forest, and diagnostic models were trained and evaluated using eight machine-learning algorithms. Immune infiltration was assessed by CIBERSORT, and cell death-related pathway activity was analyzed using ssGSEA. The expression of core MRDEGs was further validated in a SA-induced OM mouse model by RT-qPCR and Western blotting, and in human bone tissue specimens by Western blotting.
Twenty MRDEGs were identified, and five core genes, QTRT1, ABCB6, PPIF, ACSL1, and GLRX5, were selected. The LASSO-based model showed the best performance in the external evaluation cohort, with an AUC of 0.879. These genes were associated with neutrophil, macrophage, and monocyte infiltration, as well as cell death-related pathways, including ferroptosis, apoptosis, and NETosis. Mouse and human bone tissue validation further supported disease-associated expression changes of the five core genes.
This study identifies a mitochondria-related five-gene signature associated with SA-induced OM. These genes may serve as tissue-based adjunctive molecular indicators for SA-induced OM lesion assessment and provide a framework for linking mitochondrial dysfunction, immune remodeling, and regulated cell death in osteomyelitis.

articles.titulo: Late-life depletion of the gut microbiome attenuates aging-induced frailty in male mice.
articles.autores: Chandra F, Olson CA, … Hsiao EY (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Frailty summarizes aging-related decline independently of chronological age. Although the gut microbiome covaries with frailty in older populations, its causal contribution to frailty remains unclear. We profiled middle-aged (72-week-old) and young (10-week-old) male mice across six data layers including physio-behavioral phenotypes, fecal metagenomic taxa and pathways, serum lipidome, and liver and hippocampal transcriptomes. Aged mice exhibited elevated frailty, reduced motor coordination, and microbiome alterations, with members of Lactobacillus and Bacteroidia correlating with frailty. To assess microbiome dependence, we depleted the microbiome by late-life treatment with antibiotics or germ-free rearing from birth. With both, frailty in aged male mice shifted toward young-mouse values, but motor coordination and recognition memory did not, indicating selective microbiome regulation of aging phenotypes. Reduced frailty coincided with attenuated hepatic inflammatory signatures, including decreased expression of acute-phase reactants and altered fatty acid and bile acid metabolism. Microbiome depletion attenuated aging-associated lipidomic patterns, including reduced polyunsaturated-to-monounsaturated fatty acid ratio associated with diminished metabolic health. Multi-omics integration implicated lipoteichoic acid, microbial phytoestrogen metabolites, and reductions in immunomodulatory microbes in hepatic senescence, impaired bioenergetics, and inflammation. These findings suggest that the microbiome contributes to aging-induced frailty and provides new hypotheses for future mechanistic studies, including gut-liver regulation of immunometabolic function.

articles.titulo: Gain Control of Peripheral Input by Core Brain Thermosensors Drives Drosophila Thermoregulation.
articles.revista: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
articles.autores: Lazopulo S, Zlatic M, … Samuel ADT (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Temperature affects all aspects of animal physiology, rendering thermoregulation critical for survival. In Drosophila larvae, well-established peripheral thermosensors detect temperature changes and mediate thermotaxis over a broad innocuous range, but how larvae seek a specific preferred body temperature within this range remains unknown. Here we show that core thermosensors in the brain (LPBT neurons) establish this setpoint by mediating warming-evoked turning at temperatures above it. LPBTs express the warmth-activated thermosensor TrpA1(A), but are not simply cell-autonomous thermosensors. Rather, sustained LPBT responses above setpoint require both peripheral thermosensory input and TRPA1-dependent thermosensing within LPBTs. TRPA1-dependent core thermosensing provides gain control that defines the homeostatic setpoint by tuning the behavioral weights of peripheral inputs. This new conception of thermal preference reveals parallels between Drosophila and mammalian thermoregulation.

articles.titulo: Zoonotic Malaria Beyond Elimination: Making One Health Accountable.
articles.revista: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
articles.autores: Susilawati TN, Susanto H (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Zoonotic malaria challenges the assumption that interrupting human-to-human malaria transmission is sufficient to reduce the malaria burden. Plasmodium knowlesi, now the leading cause of malaria in Malaysia, shows how malaria can persist despite the elimination of indigenous human-only transmission. One Health has become the dominant response framework, but it provides limited guidance on how to allocate resources when evidence for many proposed interventions remains limited. We argue that zoonotic malaria activities should be prioritised according to the decisions they inform and their potential to reduce disease and death. Clinical readiness, including prompt recognition, referral and treatment of severe malaria, should remain the primary priority because it is the only intervention currently associated with improved clinical outcomes. Beyond clinical readiness, additional surveillance, ecological and wildlife activities should be judged by whether they trigger actionable responses rather than by alignment with the One Health framework.

articles.titulo: L-Asparaginase exposure and immune fitness in pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia: A critical evidence appraisal for immunotherapy integration.
articles.autores: Yao D, Lin X, Jiang C (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: L-asparaginase (L-ASP) is indispensable in pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), but circulating and marrow-resident immune cells encounter the same systemic amino-acid perturbation as leukemic blasts. Whether this exposure modifies the fitness of cells required for immunotherapy remains unresolved. This critical narrative review evaluates L-ASP and amino-acid-restriction evidence across T cells, natural killer cells, B cells, macrophages, and the bone-marrow niche, and relates it to blinatumomab, chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy, and checkpoint blockade. We assess intervention directness, clinical relevance, and study quality separately. T-cell studies show that asparagine supports early activation, whereas selected activated CD8⁺ states can mount an activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4)-dependent nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2) response under defined restriction conditions. Direct in-vitro asparaginase studies report differing effects on human natural killer-cell killing and should be distinguished from glutamine withdrawal or intracellular glutaminase inhibition; direct enzyme-exposure studies also identify B-cell and macrophage effects in non-pediatric-ALL models, while local marrow effects remain uncertain. Clinical regimens establish that L-ASP and immunotherapies can be used within the same treatment program, but they do not define a metabolic washout interval. We therefore distinguish serum enzyme activity, biochemical substrate recovery, and functional immune recovery. Prospective studies should link these measures to partner-specific cellular, manufacturing, and clinical endpoints. Current evidence supports testable compatibility hypotheses, not fixed scheduling rules.

articles.titulo: Challenges and Opportunities for Integrated Vector Management in Developing Countries: A Narrative Review with a Focus on Iran.
articles.autores: Dehghan O, Ghaffari J, … Azarm A (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Vector-borne diseases (VBDs), caused by pathogens transmitted through the bites of infected arthropod vectors, remain a major public health challenge in many developing countries. Environmental changes, urbanization, population mobility and health system limitations continue to sustain the transmission of these pathogens and the diseases they cause. Integrated Vector Management (IVM), recommended by the World Health Organization, provides a sustainable framework that combines evidence-based vector control interventions with surveillance, intersectoral collaboration, and community participation. However, implementation of IVM remains inconsistent, particularly in resource-limited settings.
This narrative review synthesized evidence from peer-reviewed literature indexed in PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science, supplemented by WHO technical guidance documents and regional surveillance reports published between 2000 and 2025. The review focused on IVM principles, implementation barriers, operational challenges and policy opportunities, with particular emphasis on Iran.
The review identified several interconnected barriers limiting effective IVM implementation, including unstable financing, insufficient intersectoral coordination, gaps in entomological and epidemiological surveillance, limited community participation, inadequate technical capacity and increasing insecticide resistance. Evidence from Iran demonstrates substantial progress in malaria control while highlighting ongoing challenges related to leishmaniasis, emerging Aedes-borne disease risks, resistance management, and the need for stronger integration of environmental and surveillance systems.
Achieving sustainable reductions in VBD burden will depend on long-term commitment to integrated governance, resistance-informed decision-making and context-specific strategies that enable countries such as Iran and other developing settings to build resilient vector control systems.

articles.titulo: Diversity and altitudinal distribution of avian haemosporidians (Haemoproteus, Leucocytozoon, and Plasmodium) in resident and neotropical migratory birds in Colombia.
articles.revista: International journal for parasitology. Parasites and wildlife
articles.autores: Martínez-Sánchez ET, Santana Porras JD, … Ossa-López PA (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Haemosporidians of the genera Haemoproteus, Leucocytozoon, and Plasmodium are vector-borne parasites that infect a wide range of bird species worldwide and may have significant effects on host survival. However, research conducted over the past decades has paid limited attention to ecological factors such as elevation, which is associated with the acquisition, transmission, and distribution of these parasites. In Colombia, knowledge of haemosporidian parasite diversity remains limited and fragmented. In this context, the aim of this study was to establish associations between haemosporidians and wild birds occurring at different elevations in the department of Caldas. Wild birds were captured and blood samples were collected at nine localities distributed across different elevations in four municipalities within the department. Haemosporidians were detected through microscopic examination of blood smears and molecular screening targeting the mitochondrial cytochrome b (cyt b) gene. In total, 74 samples from 45 bird species were analyzed, revealing an overall haemosporidian prevalence (Haemoproteus, Leucocytozoon, and Plasmodium) of 29.7% (n = 22). Infections were detected in 12 bird species, including residents (eleven individuals), neotropical migratory (two individuals), and introduced (nine individuals) birds. Fifteen parasite lineages were identified, including three lineages that are new to science (TURIGN01, TURFUS02, and ARRASS01). Finally, haemosporidian infections were detected across a broad elevational gradient (1021-2842 m a.s.l.), although prevalence varied considerably among localities. Furthermore, this study documents Leucocytozoon infection at 1021 m a.s.l., contributing to the growing evidence of the occurrence of this genus across a broad elevational gradient in Colombia.

articles.titulo: The Central Role of O-GlcNAcylation in Regulating Macrophages in the Pathogenesis of Periodontitis.
articles.autores: Wang Q, Wnag X, … Jiang X (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease initiated by dental plaque biofilm, characterized primarily by dysregulated host immune-inflammatory responses and progressive alveolar bone resorption, in which the dynamic M1/M2 polarization of macrophages serves as a pivotal regulatory factor. O-GlcNAcylation is a nutrient-sensitive post translational modification, and the relationship between O-GlcNAcylation and periodontitis needs further elucidation.
This article systematically reviews recent advances concerning the regulatory role of O-GlcNAcylation in macrophage-mediated periodontitis pathogenesis. Particular emphasis is placed on the bidirectional dose and site-specific effects of O-GlcNAcylation on macrophage polarization. In addition, the molecular mechanisms underlying pathological O-GlcNAcylation-mediated aggravated alveolar bone loss in diabetes-associated periodontitis are summarized.
Existing evidence identifies O-GlcNAcylation as a critical molecular hub linking metabolic derangements to periodontal osteoimmune destruction: it either potentiates M1-like pro-inflammatory responses and osteoclastogenesis, or facilitates M2-like reparative phenotypes and periodontal bone regeneration. In diabetes-associated periodontitis, aberrantly elevated O-GlcNAcylation significantly accelerates alveolar bone loss by enhancing inflammatory signaling and suppressing bone formation.
O-GlcNAcylation lays novel theoretical foundations and translational strategies for precision immuno-metabolic therapy of periodontitis, especially in patients complicated with metabolic syndrome.

articles.titulo: Extracellular vesicles at the immunometabolic interface in rheumatoid arthritis: evidence, mechanistic boundaries and translational opportunities.
articles.autores: Leng Y, Qi X (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is sustained by reciprocal interactions among immune, stromal, vascular and tissue-remodeling cells within a hypoxic, oxidant-rich and nutrient-competitive synovial environment. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) can transfer RNAs, proteins, lipids and other bioactive cargo between these compartments, but the RA-EV literature often invokes immunometabolic reprogramming without directly measuring metabolism.
We examine evidence linking EVs, immunometabolism and RA and distinguish direct metabolic effects from metabolism-linked mechanisms, context-dependent immune phenotypes and patient-derived biomarker observations. Among the endogenous studies examined, M1-macrophage EV-associated miR-155 provides a clear example in which recipient CD4 + T-cell metabolic function was measured, including extracellular acidification, oxygen consumption, lactate excretion and intracellular ATP levels. Most other endogenous studies identify metabolism-related cargo, signaling pathways or immune phenotypes without directly establishing recipient-cell metabolic reprogramming. An engineered plant vesicle formulation loaded with spermidine also altered macrophage extracellular acidification and oxygen consumption in experimental models. These findings should be distinguished from patient-derived EV associations and from engineered systems in which an exogenous drug or catalytic material may account for the principal effect.
Direct measurements of recipient-cell metabolism remain uncommon in RA-EV research. Stronger studies will require well-described EV preparations, EV- and cargo-dependence controls, functional metabolic assays, physiologically plausible dosing and validation in primary human RA systems. In the future, these approaches could inform mechanism-based patient stratification, externally validated biomarkers and targeted EV-based delivery. These are research opportunities: patient-derived EV findings have not yet established a clinically useful test, and EV-based therapy has not established clinical efficacy in RA.

articles.titulo: Laboratory Evaluation of a Non-Insecticide Multimodal Trap Using Carbon Dioxide, Lactic Acid, Ultraviolet-A Light and Sound Frequency for Aedes aegypti Control.
articles.autores: Mubarak M, Satoto TBT (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Dengue remains an important public health problem in tropical and subtropical settings. Aedes aegypti is a principal dengue vector and is highly adapted to domestic environments. Because repeated chemical-based control may contribute to insecticide resistance and environmental exposure, practical non-insecticide tools are needed. This study evaluated a non-insecticide multimodal trap integrating carbon dioxide, lactic acid, ultraviolet-A light and sound frequency for Ae. aegypti control.
This quasi-experimental study evaluated a laboratory prototype multimodal trap. A total of 2,850 female Ae. aegypti mosquitoes were used for multimodal combination testing and commercial-trap comparison after preliminary attractant optimization. The colony was obtained from the Parasitology Laboratory, Faculty of Medicine, Public Health and Nursing, Universitas Gadjah Mada, Yogyakarta, Indonesia. Non-blood-fed females aged 3-5 days were used. Each treatment included three replications of 50 mosquitoes. Outcomes were analyzed using the General Linear Model and repeated ANOVA.
Lactic acid was the most effective single attractant (78.66%). The four-mode combination produced the highest mean effectiveness (91.33%), with a maximum observed value of 98%. In the enclosed-room test, the multimodal trap performed significantly better than the Mosquito Killer BG-360 and the suction-only negative control, but not significantly better than the Photocatalyst Mosquito and Fly Trap.
The non-insecticide multimodal trap showed promising laboratory effectiveness for capturing or electrocuting Ae. aegypti. Semi-field and field trials are needed to assess operational effectiveness, feasibility, electrical safety and durability.

articles.titulo: Five-year trends in Malaria prevalence, Plasmodium species distribution, demographic patterns, and seasonal variation at Yejube health center, Baso Liben district, East Gojjam zone, Ethiopia, 2020-2024: Implications for Malaria elimination.
articles.autores: Fenta A, Dilnessa T, … Abebaw D (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Malaria remains a major global public health problem, with an estimated 282 million cases and 610,000 deaths in 2024, predominantly in the WHO African Region. Ethiopia continues to face substantial malaria transmission and has adopted an elimination strategy emphasizing surveillance, early diagnosis and treatment, and integrated vector control. Assessing local temporal, species-specific, demographic, and seasonal patterns is essential to guide targeted malaria elimination efforts.
To assess the five-year temporal trend of malaria prevalence, Plasmodium species distribution, demographic patterns, and seasonal variation among patients attending Yejube Health Center, Baso Liben District, East Gojjam Zone, Ethiopia.
A facility-based retrospective study was conducted in Yejube Health Center, Baso Liben District, East Gojjam Zone, Ethiopia, using laboratory records from January 2020 to December 2024. All individuals tested for malaria by microscopy during this period were included. Data on test results, Plasmodium species, age, sex, year, and month of diagnosis were extracted from laboratory logbooks. Data were entered in EpiData 4.2, then analyzed using SPSS 24. Descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and binary logistic regression were used to assess malaria test positivity and associated factors. Adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated, and statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.
A total of 7,806 blood films were examined from 2020 to 2024, of which 1,066 were positive for malaria, yielding an overall test positivity rate of 13.65% (95% CI: 12.91-14.44%). Annual positivity declined from 20.08% in 2020 to 4.95% in 2023, followed by a resurgence to 14.66% in 2024. Plasmodium falciparum accounted for 49.6% of confirmed cases, followed by P. vivax (43.3%) and mixed-species infections (7.0%). Although P. falciparum predominated in 2020, P. vivax predominated from 2021 onward. Malaria test positivity was significantly higher among males than females (16.7% vs. 10.1%; p < 0.001) and differed significantly across age groups (p < 0.001). Monthly positivity peaked in October (21.5%) and November (20.3%), with the lowest rate in February (3.9%). In multivariable logistic regression, males had higher odds of malaria positivity than females (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 1.79, 95% CI: 1.56-2.06). Compared with individuals aged ≥60 years, the odds were higher among children aged under five years (AOR = 9.27, 95% CI: 1.27-67.77), individuals aged 15-29 years (AOR = 8.39, 95% CI: 1.15-61.27), and those aged 30-59 years (AOR = 9.60, 95% CI: 1.31-70.25). Compared with August, the odds of malaria positivity were significantly higher in September, October, November, and May, but significantly lower in February.
Malaria test positivity at Yejube Health Center declined from 2020 to 2023 before resurging in 2024. Although P. falciparum predominated overall, P. vivax was the leading species from 2021 onward. Positivity was associated with sex, age, and month of diagnosis, with peaks in October and a secondary increase in May. These findings underscore the need for sustained surveillance and locally tailored malaria control strategies.
Strengthen malaria surveillance and seasonal preparedness, particularly before peak-positivity periods. Tailor prevention and health education to males and higher-risk age groups, and improve P. vivax diagnosis, treatment, and relapse prevention. Further studies incorporating population-based, meteorological, and entomological data are recommended to clarify transmission patterns and guide malaria control and elimination efforts.

articles.titulo: The Indian Jumping Ant Harpegnathos saltator as a Model to Study Brain Plasticity and Epigenetics.
articles.autores: Moreno-Medina S, Kuang M, … Khan S (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Epigenetic regulation of gene expression plays a central role in brain plasticity during development and adulthood, and in response to the environment. While vertebrate models have provided important insights into these processes, systems that exhibit inducible and reversible plasticity throughout adulthood offer unique opportunities to investigate how environmental and social cues drive long-lasting changes in the brain, behavior, and physiology. Eusocial insects are well suited for such studies because individuals sharing nearly identical genomes can develop distinct behavioral, physiological, and reproductive phenotypes through socially regulated molecular, endocrine, and epigenetic pathways. The Indian jumping ant, Harpegnathos saltator, is of particular interest because adult workers can reversibly transition into a queen-like reproductive state called the gamergate. This transition involves coordinated behavioral, physiological, and neural changes, including alterations in gene expression, neuropeptide levels, and brain cellular composition. Despite the growing number of research groups using Harpegnathos, standardized and systematic protocols for working with these insects are lacking. Here, we provide a general overview of Harpegnathos, describe the worker-gamergate transition, and discuss its utility for studying brain plasticity and neuroepigenetic regulation. We further summarize the genomic and epigenomic resources that have been developed to date for the molecular characterization of brain plasticity in this species, and highlight the need for a consolidated set of standardized protocols to support reproducible research using Harpegnathos Such approaches will lower technical barriers to working with Harpegnathos and further establish it as a powerful model for linking social behavior, brain plasticity, and genome regulation.

articles.titulo: Non-invasive in vivo imaging assessment of retinal microglia-like cells in diabetic retinopathy by adaptive optics optical coherence tomography.
articles.autores: Kunze L, Brunner E, … Pollreisz A (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a microvascular, neurodegenerative and inflammatory disorder characterised by retinal microglial activation. In this study, we used adaptive optics optical coherence tomography (AO-OCT) to assess microglia-like cell morphology and density at the inner limiting membrane (ILM) in vivo in eyes with DR and healthy controls.
Eleven eyes from nine patients with DR and seven eyes from seven healthy controls were examined using a prototype AO-OCT system. Volumetric images were acquired over a 4°×4° field of view at five standardised retinal locations extending from the superior vascular arcade to the parafovea. For ultrastructural reference, a retinal sample from the foveal region of a 51-year-old donor was analysed using serial block-face scanning electron microscopy (SBFSEM).
Retinal microglia-like cells were consistently visualised at the ILM in all participants using single-volume AO-OCT imaging. High-resolution imaging allowed identification of distinct morphological phenotypes consistent with histological findings and SBFSEM observations. The proportion of cells with a reactive morphology was higher in eyes with DR than in controls (median 51% vs. 16%). Overall cell density did not differ significantly between groups but showed considerable interindividual variability. In contrast, a greater proportion of cells were embedded within the ILM in DR eyes compared with controls (median 90% vs. 53%). SBFSEM provided detailed ultrastructural characterisation, revealing fine processes approximately 100-400 nm in diameter extending from the soma of microglia with a reactive morphology, a feature not previously reported.
AO-OCT enables three-dimensional, quantitative assessment of microglia-like cell morphology and distribution in healthy eyes and eyes with DR. Eyes with DR showed an increased proportion of cells with a reactive morphology and a greater proportion of cells embedded within the ILM, suggesting increased retinal immune activation. These findings support AO-OCT as a tool for investigating retinal inflammatory changes in DR and other retinal disorders.

articles.titulo: Impact of Mass Testing, Treatment, and Tracking Interventions on the Genetic Diversity of Plasmodium falciparum in Two Endemic Ghanaian Communities.
articles.revista: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
articles.autores: Asante A, Asa-Atiemo CKM, … Amoah LE (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Asymptomatic malaria infections sustain transmission in endemic settings and may undermine elimination efforts. Mass testing, treatment, and tracking (MTTT) target both symptomatic and asymptomatic infections, but its impact on Plasmodium falciparum (P. falciparum) genetic diversity remains poorly understood. In the present study, temporal changes in P. falciparum merozoite surface protein 2 (msp2) genetic diversity and multiplicity of infection (MOI) were assessed during repeated MTTT interventions in two high-transmission Ghanaian communities. A total of 566 dried blood spot (DBS) samples, previously confirmed as P. falciparum-positive via photo-induced electron transfer polymerase chain reaction (PCR), were randomly selected from asymptomatic individuals in Obom (N = 278) and Kofi Kwei (N = 288) during three MTTT rounds conducted in January, May, and September 2021. Parasite DNA was extracted, and msp2 genotyping was performed using gel-based nested PCR to determine the 3D7 and FC27 allele diversity and MOI. The 3D7 allelic family predominated at both sites (Obom: 71%; Kofi Kwei: 68%). Multiplicity of infection declined significantly between the first and third MTTT rounds in Obom (1.80 to 1.10; P <0.0001) and Kofi Kwei (1.60 to 1.30; P = 0.0007). Despite reduced MOI, allelic diversity remained high, with 3D7 fragments ranging from ∼200 to 500 base pairs (bp) and FC27 fragments ranging from 300 to 500 bp. Allelic distributions did not differ significantly across age groups (3D7: P = 0.95; FC27: P = 0.59). A reduction in infection complexity was observed across the repeated MTTT intervention rounds, whereas parasite msp2 allelic diversity remained relatively high. These findings highlight the importance of integrating molecular surveillance into malaria control programs and targeting asymptomatic infections to reduce transmission reservoirs.

articles.titulo: Seasonal mass vaccination with R21/Matrix-M against malaria in The Gambia and Burkina Faso: an open-label, cluster-randomised, controlled trial.
articles.autores: Dabira ED, Natama HM, … D'Alessandro U (25 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
The R21/Matrix-M (R21) malaria vaccine candidate, recommended by WHO for use in young children, could be extended to the whole population. Seasonal mass vaccination (SMV) before peak malaria transmission could be a promising tool to accelerate progress towards malaria elimination. We aimed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of SMV with R21 in two malaria-endemic settings in west Africa.
This open-label, cluster-randomised, controlled trial was conducted in The Gambia, a setting with low-to-moderate seasonal transmission, and Burkina Faso, a setting with intense seasonal transmission. 54 medium-sized villages (30 in The Gambia and 24 in Burkina Faso) were randomly assigned (1:1) by use of computer-restricted randomisation to receive either SMV with R21 (intervention group) or no SMV (control group). All study villages received national standard malaria control interventions. In the intervention group, residents who were aged 5 months and older, willing to comply with trial procedures, and could provide written informed consent (from parents or guardians for children aged <18 years plus assent for children aged 12-17 years) were eligible for vaccination. The intervention was delivered as three monthly doses of 5 μg (participants aged <15 years) or 10 μg (participants aged ≥15 years) R21 plus 50 μg of Matrix-M. The primary outcome was malaria prevalence at peak transmission, defined as the proportion of participants with Plasmodium falciparum infection assessed by quantitative PCR. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06578572) and the Pan-African Clinical Trials Registry (PACTR202404544467702), and is ongoing.
The intervention was delivered between May 30, and Aug 21, 2024. A cross-sectional survey to estimate the primary endpoint was conducted between Nov 18 and Dec 6, 2024. The population available for vaccination varied across the three rounds. In The Gambia, among 4311 total residents in intervention villages, 2565 (59·5%) received three vaccine doses; in Burkina Faso, among 6235 total residents in intervention villages, 4072 (65·3%) received three vaccine doses. SMV with R21 reduced the odds of malaria infection by 70% (adjusted odds ratio 0·30 [95% CI 0·20-0·44]; p<0·0001) in The Gambia and by 25% (0·75 [95% CI 0·58-0·98]; p=0·036) in Burkina Faso. In The Gambia, prevalence decreased across all age groups, whereas in Burkina Faso the largest effect was observed in children younger than 5 years. The vaccine was safe and well tolerated. 651 adverse events were reported in 581 (13·5%) vaccine recipients in The Gambia, and 795 adverse events were reported in 705 (11·3%) vaccine recipients in Burkina Faso. Among 69 serious adverse events reported overall, only one was considered related to vaccination (febrile convulsions in a female participant aged 8 years after the second dose in The Gambia).
SMV with R21 reduced malaria prevalence in both settings. It could become an additional strategy for malaria control in endemic areas of seasonal transmission. In low-to-moderate transmission settings, the vaccine could accelerate progress towards elimination; in high-transmission areas it could further reduce the malaria burden.

articles.titulo: Protocol for measuring antibody-dependent enhancement and neutralization using reporter virus particles.
articles.autores: Sheetz A, Frey N, … Doranz BJ (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Reporter virus particles (RVPs) are non-replicative, antigenically equivalent viral particles that enable BSL-2-compliant virology research using standard optical detection instrumentation. Here, we present a protocol for measuring neutralization and antibody-dependent enhancement (ADE) of flavivirus infection using dengue virus (DENV) RVPs. For both neutralization and ADE assays, we describe the steps for preparing sera and antibodies, pre-incubating with RVPs to allow immune complex formation, applying to BHK DC-SIGN or K562 cells, and quantifying reporter signal as a readout of viral entry. For complete details on the use and execution of this protocol, please refer to Grinyo-Escuer et al.1.

articles.titulo: HIV proteins disrupt a network of phosphatidylinositol (4,5)-bisphosphate binding sites on the dopamine transporter to regulate amphetamine behaviours.
articles.autores: Zhu Y, Parwana D, … Galli A (13 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Amphetamine (AMPH) use has been linked to human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) transmission because HIV can spread through unprotected sex that is associated with AMPH use disorder (AUD). Thus, AUD and HIV have been termed a double epidemic. In this bidirectional relationship, the role played by AUD in HIV-dependent neuropathogenesis is well documented. By contrast, how HIV infection regulates the development of AUD remains elusive. In rodents, expression of HIV viral proteins, such as the trans-activator of transcription (Tat), enhances AMPH escalation (i.e. a progressive intensification of drug use), a Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-5) criteria for addiction. In humans, HIV infection increases AMPH frequency of use, as well as the total amount used. Thus, it is possible that HIV/HIV proteins promote the progression of AUD. AMPH-associated behaviours stem, at least in part, from the ability of AMPH to reverse the dopamine (DA) transporter (DAT) function, causing non-vesicular DA release (NVDR) and an increase in extracellular DA. Previously, we provided the first evidence that specific domains of DAT engage in direct association with the plasma membrane lipid, phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2). These interactions are essential for AMPH-induced NVDR and specific behaviours. HIV Tat is a protein that binds PIP2 through its basic domain. We demonstrate that Tat impairs NVDR by disrupting the network of PIP2 binding sites on DAT. Our study provides an atomic scale mechanistic description on how Tat disrupts human DAT/PIP2 association and blunts AMPH-induced NVDR. Using Drosophila as an animal model, we show that Tat by blunting NVDR in the setting of AUD promotes AMPH escalation. KEY POINTS: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) trans-activator of transcription (Tat) impairs non-vesicular dopamine (DA) release (NVDR) by disrupting the network of PIP2 binding sites on human Da transporter (DAT). Our study provides an atomic scale mechanistic description on how Tat disrupts human DAT/phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate association and blunts amphetamine (AMPH)-induced NVDR. We associate Tat blunting of NVDR to the ability of Tat to foster AMPH escalation, using Drosophila as an animal model.
